name: Hong Kong
tagline: English-taught, IB-literate, and the early rounds close in November
summary: Hong Kong's universities teach in English and read the IB directly. An EU/EEA student is a non-local applicant: you apply to each university on its own site, not through JUPAS. The early rounds close in November 2026, on predicted grades. Fees are high, about HK$250,000 to 280,000 (about €28,000–31,400 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a year at HKU.
whyConsider: HKU, CUHK and HKUST teach in English and take the IB as a standard qualification.
HKU keeps applications open after IB results day, until 25 August 2027. Of the five universities covered here, it is the only one.
watchOuts: The first rounds close from 12 November 2026 (CUHK) to 25 November (HKU, HKUST), with CityU on 15 and PolyU on 17 November. Most places are decided there, on predicted grades.
Each university is a separate application, with its own fee and its own dates.
Dates and fees here are for HKU, HKUST, CUHK, PolyU and CityU only. Check every other university on its own site.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: Set per university and programme. CUHK's general minimum is 30 of 45.
notes: Offers made on predicted grades are conditional on the final diploma.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Most programmes at the main universities.
language.englishProof: Set per university. CUHK accepts an IB English grade of 4. Check each of the others.

feeContext.summary: Hong Kong has no EU category. An EU/EEA citizen is non-local and pays the non-local fee.
2027/28 non-local tuition: HKU HK$280,000 a year in STEM faculties and HK$250,000 in the others; HKUST HK$260,000; PolyU HK$240,000; CUHK HK$230,000.

sectorLandscape.summary: Eight universities are funded by the University Grants Committee (UGC). Beside them are the Academy for Performing Arts, which is publicly funded outside the UGC, and a group of self-financing universities. Below degree level, associate degrees and higher diplomas are a large route of their own.

routes.what: HKU, CUHK, HKUST, PolyU, CityU, HKBU, Lingnan and EdUHK. These are the universities most students mean by Hong Kong. Each admits non-local students directly, on its own dates.

routes.localName: The Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts
routes.what: Degrees in dance, drama, music, film and theatre production. Admission is by audition or portfolio.
routes.note: Its admissions pages are not covered in detail here.

routes.what: Hang Seng University, Metropolitan University, Shue Yan University and THEi. Degree-awarding, without recurrent government funding, and more career-focused than the UGC eight.
routes.note: Their entry for non-local IB students is not covered here.

routes.what: Two-year programmes at community colleges and institution-linked schools. Many Hong Kong students use them to top up into a degree later. Foreign guides rarely mention this route.

notes: Audited 2026-09-24 (docs/research/audit/hk.md): CityU's dates and fees were read in a browser; HKUST, CUHK and PolyU 2027/28 fees added.
Written to the publication floor by the Greece, China and Hong Kong pass on 2026-09-23. One direct route covers every institution because every one of them admits non-local students directly.

Not established: the dates at HKBU, Lingnan, EdUHK, HKAPA and the self-financing universities. The Concourse site (cspe.edu.hk) renders its institution list in JavaScript and serves a broken TLS chain.
